questions.q: What is the difference between a program and a process?
options: A program is a file of instructions on the disk; a process is that program running right now
A process is a file; a program is running
A program runs on the CPU; a process runs on the disk
questions.explain: One program file (like email_worker.py) can become many processes, each with its own PID and memory.

questions.q: The price updater thread changes a price in memory. Who sees the new price at once?
options: The other threads of the same process
questions.explain: Threads of one process share the same memory. Other processes have their own memory and don't see it. That is why the order emails still said ₹999.

questions.q: 10 threads each do: read the stock, check it, write stock − 1. Bazaar sells 10 earbuds but had only 8. What is this bug called, and what fixes it?
options: A memory leak; fix it with more RAM
A race condition; fix it with a lock (or a database lock)
A zombie; fix it with kill -9
A slow disk; fix it with an SSD
questions.explain: The threads mixed their read and write steps. A lock lets only one thread at a time do all three steps.

questions.q: You run kill 9 (the PID) on an email-worker. What happens to bazaar-backend?
options: It keeps running; its supervisor even starts a new email-worker
questions.explain: Processes are isolated. A crash stays inside that one process. In the lab, the supervisor saw the exit and started a new worker with a new PID.

questions.q: top shows bazaar-backend at 100% CPU on an 8-core computer. What does that mean?
options: The whole computer is completely full
One core is fully busy; the other 7 are free
questions.explain: In top, 100% means one full core, measured just now. With 8 cores, the maximum is 800%.

questions.q: (Going deeper) What is the difference between kill <pid> and kill -9 <pid>?
options: kill sends SIGTERM ("please stop", can be handled); kill -9 sends SIGKILL ("stop now", can't be caught)
questions.explain: Always try plain kill (SIGTERM) first, so the program can finish its work. SIGKILL gives it no chance.

questions.q: (Going deeper) A Bazaar container stopped with "exit code 137". What does that tell you?
options: It received SIGKILL (128 + 9), often because it ran out of memory or ignored SIGTERM
questions.explain: Shells and Docker show "killed by signal N" as 128 + N. 137 = SIGKILL, 143 = SIGTERM.

questions.q: (Going deeper) ps shows STAT = Z and <defunct> for a process. What is it?
options: A zombie: it has finished, but its parent has not collected its exit code yet
A process waiting for the disk
questions.explain: A zombie uses no CPU. It disappears when the parent calls wait(). Many zombies mean the parent has a bug.
